author: Rahul kp
title: PERT Time
simple_words: When activity time is uncertain, PERT takes three guesses and finds one weighted average time.

definitions.meaning: a is the shortest time if all goes well. b is the longest time if almost everything goes wrong.
definitions.note: a is the minimum, b is the maximum

definitions.meaning: The time the activity usually takes under normal conditions. It is the most probable estimate.
definitions.note: m gets the heavy weight of 4

key_points: PERT is used when activity times are ==uncertain==, such as in research or new projects.
Expected time (te) is a weighted average of a, m and b, using beta distribution weights.
Variance shows the uncertainty of an activity: a wider gap between b and a means higher variance.
Critical path is found using te values; !!project variance uses critical activities only!!.

formulas.name: Expected time of an activity
formulas.legend: te = expected time; a = optimistic; m = most likely; b = pessimistic

formulas.name: Variance of an activity
formulas.legend: σ² = variance; b − a = range of estimates; 36 = 6 squared

formulas.name: Probability of completion (Z value)
formulas.legend: Ts = scheduled time; Te = expected project time (critical path total); Σσ² = sum of critical activity variances

insight.text: Add the variances of critical activities, then take the square root to get the project standard deviation.

memory_trick.explanation: Weights are 1 for a, 4 for m, 1 for b. They total 6, so divide by 6. Variance uses the gap (b − a) over 6, squared.

steps: Add te on critical path = Te
Find σ² of critical activities, add
exam_tip: In MCQs, first check whether the question asks for te, variance or standard deviation, then pick the matching formula.

doubt.question: Why is m multiplied by 4 and not a or b?
doubt.answer: The most likely time is assumed to be the most probable value, so it gets more weight. a and b are rare extremes and get weight 1 each.

mistakes.wrong: Using (a + m + b) / 3 for expected time
mistakes.right: PERT uses te = (a + 4m + b) / 6. The simple average ignores the weights.
That is the standard deviation. Variance = [(b − a) / 6]².

mistakes.wrong: Adding variances of all activities for the project
mistakes.right: Add variances of ==critical path== activities only.

mistakes.wrong: Adding standard deviations of critical activities
mistakes.right: Add the variances first, then take the square root for project standard deviation.

reviewer_note: In the Z formula legend, the denominator is the square root of the sum of critical path variances. The square_root flag is false because the root is written in the denominator text only.
